title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops & Top Support Issues
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for the Developer Experience (DevEx) team to author and maintain SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site runbooks, and the canonical fixes list for top support issues. It centralizes ownership, the publication workflow, and a prioritized list of recurring customer problems with reproducible fixes.

Audience: SDK writers, developer advocates, support engineers, solutions engineers, and product owners.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-value for new developers through consistent quickstarts and examples.
- Keep canonical fixes up-to-date to reduce MTTR for top support issues.
- Make docs contributions low-friction and reviewable at scale.
- Ensure docs are testable, versioned, and runnable in CI.

Ownership and Roles

- Owner: DevEx Docs Team (primary contact: Asha Patel).
- Maintainers: SDK owners (Python, TypeScript, Go), DevRel for examples, Support for canonical fixes.
- Reviewers: API product manager + runtime engineering for correctness.
- Publishing: DevEx releases content to the docs site; release tagged in repo and mirrored to Confluence.

Doc Types and Where They Live

- SDK Guides (folder: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates): language-specific guides, install, auth, best practices.
- Quickstarts & Templates: minimal runnable examples that get a dev from zero to a response in 5 minutes.
- API Examples: concise curl + Python/TS/Go examples for common flows (chat, streaming, embeddings, function/tool calling).
- Docs Site Operating Procedures: step-by-step publishing, CI checks, and rollback.
- Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes: triage guide, reproducible steps, root cause, and remediation.

Standards for All Docs

1) Tone and Structure
- Start with a one-paragraph summary.
- Provide a short prerequisite checklist (SDK version, API key, region).
- Use numbered quickstart steps and copy-paste runnable code blocks.
- Add a Troubleshooting section with the canonical fixes (see below).
- End with Related Links and a short FAQ.

2) Metadata (required fields for every Confluence doc)
- title, summary (1-2 sentences), author, owner_team, reviewers, labels, created_at, last_updated, confidentiality.

3) Code Samples
- All code samples must be kept in the central examples repo and referenced by snippet id.
- Each sample must include a minimal environment (Python: venv + requirements.txt; Node: package.json).
- Each sample must be runnable in < 3 minutes on a dev laptop.

4) Versioning
- Include SDK version and API compatibility header. E.g., "SDK: @redwood/sdk-python v1.4.x — API v2025-12".

Quickstart Template (copyable)

Title: Quickstart: <language> — Hello Redwood API
Summary: 2 lines describing what the quickstart achieves.
Prerequisites:
- Redwood account + API key set as REDWOOD_API_KEY
- SDK: <package>@<version>
- Node 18+/Python 3.10+ as applicable
Steps:
1. Install the SDK
   - CLI command(s)
2. Create a minimal config (show env var or config file)
3. Run the example (full code block)
4. Validate output and common next steps
Troubleshooting: common errors + links to canonical fixes
Related links: full SDK guide, API reference, examples repo link

API Example Requirements Table

| Flow | Required Scope | Example Snippet ID | Notes |
| Chat | chat.write | py-chat-hello | Streaming example in separate snippet |
| Embeddings | embed.compute | py-emb-hello | Show batching tips |
| Rerank | rerank.score | js-rerank-sample | Use small dataset example |

(Represented here as markdown-style table for authoring; final Confluence table uses native table macro.)

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publish + rollback)

1) Authoring and Local Preview
- Branch off main: docs/<short-desc>-<issue-id>.
- Add markdown + snippet references. Run local site: yarn start-docs.
- Run lint: yarn docs:lint (checks broken links, frontmatter, snippet presence).

2) PR and Review
- Create PR with checklist (PR template ensures metadata present).
- Required approvers: SDK owner + DevEx tech writer + product manager.
- CI gates: docs:lint, snippet tests, spellcheck.

3) Publishing
- Merge to main triggers deploy to staging. QA validates sample snippets run and smoke tests (curl sample against staging runtime).
- After 48h staging verification, schedule deploy to prod during docs release window (Tue 09:00–11:00 PT).
- Update Confluence page last_updated, add change note in release notes.

4) Rollback
- If a publish causes regressions, file an expedited rollback PR reverting the merge commit. QA verifies revert on staging then triggers prod rollback.
- Notify #devex-docs and on-call support.

Maintaining the Canonical Fixes List (Top Support Issues)

Process:
1. Triage: Support tags issues with "canonical-fix" label and assigns to owner.
2. Repro: Reproduce in a minimal example and add a failing test to the examples repo.
3. Fix & Doc: Document the root cause, the remediation steps, a short command to fix, and a post-fix validation command.
4. Publish: Add the fix to the Confluence canonical fixes page and link to quickstart if example changed.
5. Measure: After publishing, track ticket reopen rate and time-to-close over 30 days; if not improved by 20% escalate to engineering.

Top Support Issues (as of last_updated)

1) Authentication errors: "401: invalid API key"
- Root cause: mis-set environment variable or using an expired key.
- Canonical fix: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<key> (Linux/mac) or setx REDWOOD_API_KEY <key> (Windows).
- Validation: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .status
- Notes: Support must confirm key scopes include the requested API (chat/embed).

2) Streaming responses stall or disconnect mid-stream
- Root cause: client-side socket timeouts or proxy buffering (NGINX default buffers).
- Canonical fix: Ensure the client sets a read timeout > 90s for long streams; in NGINX, set proxy_buffering off and proxy_read_timeout 300s for streaming routes.
- Validation: Reproduce with stream length 4096 tokens and confirm continuous chunked responses.

3) High tail latency for synchronous batch requests
- Root cause: batching policy mismatch — requests hitting the burst path cause head-of-line delays.
- Canonical fix: Recommend switching to async consumption (webhook or polling) for >32 concurrent long-context requests or configure SDK batching: set MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=2048 and MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8.
- Validation: Run perf-smoke script in examples repo: ./scripts/perf-smoke --concurrency=50 --flow=chat

4) Mismatched model behavior after rollout (regression)
- Root cause: rollout used a model variant without passing eval prompt sets.
- Canonical fix: Revert rollout to previous variant, run regression eval on staging prompt set, and only re-roll after meeting QA thresholds (>= 98% pass rate on critical prompts).
- Validation: Compare embeddings/LLM outputs with eval hash and generate regression report.

5) Embeddings batching or memory OOM on CPU hosts
- Root cause: too-large batch size for available memory or missing quantized float path.
- Canonical fix: Lower batch size to 16 or enable model quantization profile: QUANT_PROFILE=fp16-a10 (team must confirm compatibility).
- Validation: Run small embedding job and confirm peak RSS < 85% of host RAM.

Canonical Fix Entry Template (every fix must include)
- Title (short)
- Symptom (exact error text or observable behavior)
- Root cause (one sentence)
- Step-by-step remediation (numbered)
- Commands / code snippets (copy-paste)
- Verification steps
- Owner and last_updated

Example API Examples (minimal, copy/paste)

Curl (chat completion)

curl -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions

Python (async streaming)

# requirements: redwood-sdk>=1.4.0
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
    async for chunk in client.stream_chat("redwood-chat-1", [{"role":"user","content":"Tell me a joke."}]):
        print(chunk.text, end="")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Docs Testing and CI Requirements

- Every docs PR that introduces or changes a code snippet must include a snippet test in the examples repo. CI runs snippets in an isolated ephemeral environment (GH Actions or ephemeral container).
- Linting: frontmatter and link checks are mandatory.
- Accessibility: images must include alt text.

Metrics and SLAs for Docs Health

- Freshness: pages with core SDK examples must be updated within 3 months of an SDK major version bump.
- Coverage: 100% of public SDK methods used in quickstarts should have at least one example.
- Stability: canonical-fix pages should reduce repeat incidents for the same root cause by 30% within 60 days.

On-call and Escalation for Docs Regression

- Primary: DevEx on-call for docs (rotating).
- If a docs change causes production user-facing regression: escalate to runtime on-call after 30 minutes of triage and open an incident.

Frequently Asked Questions (short)

Q: Where do I add a new language quickstart?
A: Create a PR in the docs repo under /examples/<language>/quickstarts and add a snippet id. Follow the quickstart template above.

Q: Who approves changes to canonical fixes?
A: Support + runtime engineer responsible for the service must sign off; DevEx publishes.

Appendix: Useful Commands

- Local docs preview: yarn start-docs
- Lint: yarn docs:lint
- Run example smoke tests: ./examples/scripts/run-all-smoke.sh
- Reproduce auth health check: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .

- Examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples (internal)
